input.description: User-supplied case summary and AI-generated statutory analysis; leads, not authority.

corrections: Section 58 reasonable-excuse examples are in 58(3A)(a) and (b)(i)-(ii), not 3B/3C.
Section 118 imposes an evidential burden; the prosecution must disprove the defence beyond reasonable doubt once sufficiently raised.
No automatic title-based liability or claim that the offence is strict liability.
Bel: corrected citation to [2021] EWCA Crim 1461; physical book and December 2018 Amazon purchase recorded in judgment, not an electronic-copy assumption.
John: corrected citation to [2022] EWCA Crim 54; six acquittals retained; appellate reasoning includes unlawful sentence structure.
Howarth: original 54-month custodial term reduced to 45 months on 24 November 2022; additional one-year licence retained.
Walker and Creagh: acquittals do not reveal jurors' reasoning or establish universal exemptions.
Cristea: distinguish possession conviction from police account of suspected attack planning in the wider group.
Smith: use 2017 as recorded in the Independent Reviewer's note rather than supplied 2016 date.
Amazon availability is supported as a dated claim, not certified current stock or edition identity.
not_adopted: Operational excerpts and reliability claims about the manual
Outcome prediction matrix, including mental illness as an automatic route to conviction
Additional Brown, McGee and Scott case narratives pending separate verification
source_access_notes: National Archives Howarth and John judgments and revised sections 58/118 retrieved from official XML endpoints because web reader could not open HTML.
Bel judgment read as a court transcript hosted by Crimeline; National Archives endpoint was unavailable.
Existing source pages are linked, not mirrored manuals.
